messages:
Maya: Quick question — for tenants with strict data residency, if their primary region goes down do we a) fail the request, or b) allow fallback to a non-resident region with redaction & explicit consent? Need a short decision so product can wire UI/state.
Alex: My instinct: default to fail-closed. But provide an opt-in `soft_fallback` for tenants that signed a specific TOS clause.
Liam: We already have a per-tenant field shape in db: `residency_policy: strict|prefer|soft`. Does `soft` imply consent recorded?
Maya: Example config I had in mind:
```json
{"residency_policy":"soft","soft_fallback_consented":true,"consent_ts":"2024-11-02T12:00:00Z"}
```
Sophia: Legal note: `soft_fallback_consented` must be an explicit checkbox in the console + audit trail. Cookie-style implied consent won't cut it for GDPR/DPAs.
Ken: From a systems POV we *can* route to another region and run a redaction transform before returning results, but tradeoffs: higher latency, cache miss (KV cache locality lost), and potential consistency issues.
Ken: Also KMS & key residency matters — we can't decrypt customer data if keys are region-locked. That needs a separate emergency key-transfer flow or escrow.
Maya: Good point. If fallback requires transferring keys we need legal + ops signoff.
Alex: Proposal: implement `soft_fallback` as opt-in, with constraints: 1) customer enables via console + signed TOS, 2) every fallback event is recorded and surfaced in console and billing, 3) fallback responses include header `X-Residency-Fallback: true` and reason code.
Liam: Implementation note: add header `X-Residency-Fallback: soft|strict` and `X-Residency-Fallback-Reasons: region-unavailable, emergency`. Also emit telemetry event `residency.fallback` with tenant id and hash of affected user ids.
SRE-bot: deploy scheduled: routing-proxy v2.14 -> staging at 03:30 UTC (today).
Ops: Playbook update required: how to quarantine KMS keys and who approves emergency key transfer. @security please chime in.
Tara: Security POV: emergency key transfer is high-risk. Prefer: 1) avoid decrypting resident data outside region, 2) if we must provide service, use redaction-at-ingress based on hashed identifiers, 3) require legal/ops approval per event.
Sophia: So legal is comfortable with soft fallback if: (a) explicit consent in contract, (b) clear UI, (c) auditable events, (d) limited data exposure & retention controls.
Maya: Action items I hear: 1) Product to define soft_fallback contract & console checkbox (Alex), 2) Schema + header spec (Liam), 3) SRE prototype redaction pipeline + perf/cost estimate (Ken + SRE team), 4) Legal signoff & approval flow (Sophia), 5) Security runbook for KMS/escrow (Tara).
Alex: I'll own the product text & the console UX.
Liam: I'll add header spec + telemetry schema PR.
Ken: SRE team will prototype a redaction shim and measure latency delta.
Sophia: I'll draft contract language and sample consent clause.
Tara: I'll draft a minimal emergency access policy and required approvers list.
Maya: One more question — are people ok with emitting fallback events to logs if we hash PII and limit retention?
Tara: Fine if hashed and retention is short (7-30d depending on region). Also no free-text dumps.
Maya: Great. I'll file an RFC follow-up with checklist and link to this thread. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
